title: A multimodal dataset of EEG, eye-tracking, and physiological signals during smartphone interaction
description: A multimodal dataset of simultaneous 64-channel EEG, head-mounted eye-tracking, photoplethysmography (PPG), and galvanic skin response (GSR) recordings from 23 healthy adults. Participants took part in a naturalistic smartphone use condition and a standardized video viewing condition. Hardware TTL pulses synchronize the EEG and eye-tracking streams for temporal alignment across modalities.
methods_description: Participants wore a 64-channel EEG cap and a head-mounted eye tracker with simultaneous PPG and GSR recording. They completed a 10-minute free smartphone use condition on their personal devices and a 5-minute standardized video viewing condition on a monitor. Session boundaries were marked with TTL pulses (five pulses at ~1 s intervals, plus pulses every 20 s) embedded in both the EEG and eye-tracking streams.
